## Why

Split from S594 (Jon chose 'Closure + gate, revert named tests', session 8d711f67, 2026-11-27). It carries three changes to the `## Base overlays` section, all owner-decided.

1. S640: an overlay command runs a whole package (`internal/engine/baseoverlay.go:161`). The section gets one `-run` line for each test in the changed test files, so a reviewer runs one test per command and reads only its result (adj 663, `base-overlays.per-test-and-vet-sample`, option per-test-live).
2. adj 632: reviewers had to build a probe overlay to see which path form real `go vet` prints (S634 evidence: `vet: internal/engine/round.go:628:19: ...`). The section quotes the first line of a real vet failure from its own overlays. It omits the sample when no vet fails (adj 663).
3. adj 655, folded in by Jon in session 8d711f67: when the S594/S634 closure also reverts a test file, the new tests in it do not run (S629 overlay-2 reverted `brief_test.go` with `round.go`). ork also offers an overlay that reverts only the product file and keeps the slice's tests, so they show red by compile error or by assertion (adj 664, `base-overlays.product-only-overlay`, option keep-tests).

Owner decisions, 2026-11-28: adj 669 (supersedes adj 663: per-test lines use -run TestName unanchored, because S610 denies $-anchored -run for read-only roles; cap 20 with a left-out count; live vet sample) and adj 664 (a product-only overlay keeps the new tests, red by compile error). S640, adj 632 and adj 655 are covered here.

## Failing tests

All tests are in `internal/engine/baseoverlay_test.go` (entry reader `baseOverlayEntries` at line 103) and use `ucsReviewerHarness` (it writes real files under the worktree) with vet routes added. A per-test or product-only sub-line is an indented line, `  - ...`, inside its entry's string, so `baseOverlayEntries` (lines starting with "- `") still counts one entry per file.

Per-test lines:
- TestBaseOverlayPerTestLines: `a.go` and `a_test.go` are changed and vet passes. `a_test.go` holds `TestOne`, `TestTwo`, a helper func, `TestMain`, a `BenchmarkX` and a method named `TestM`. The entry for `a.go` is followed by exactly two sub-lines, in source order, each `go -C W test -overlay TMP/overlay-1.json -count=1 -run TestOne ./internal/x` (then `TestTwo`). No line has a pipe.
- TestBaseOverlayPerTestLinesOnlySamePackage: a changed test file in `internal/y` adds no line under the entry for `internal/x/a.go`.
- TestBaseOverlayPerTestLinesSkipRevertedTestFile: vet names `a_test.go`, so the closure reverts it. Its tests get no per-test lines, because they do not run under that overlay.
- TestBaseOverlayPerTestLinesUnreadableFileIsSilent: a changed test file missing from disk, or one that does not parse, adds no lines and no "Check incomplete" text. The entry is unchanged.
- TestBaseOverlayPerTestLinesLimit: more tests than baseOverlayLimit (20, adj 669) list the first LIMIT lines for the section and a line "N more test lines were left out (ork lists at most LIMIT)."

Product-only overlay:
- TestBaseOverlayProductOnlyOverlayWhenTestFileReverted: with the closure reverting `a_test.go`, `overlay-1-product.json` exists and its Replace holds only `a.go` (not `a_test.go`, not other closure files). A sub-line under the entry gives `go -C W test -overlay TMP/overlay-1-product.json -count=1 ./internal/x`. The product-only overlay gets no vet call and no automatic test run.
- TestBaseOverlayNoProductOnlyOverlayWithoutRevertedTest: with no test file reverted, no `overlay-N-product.json` is written and no such sub-line appears.
- TestBaseOverlayProductOnlyOverlayMapsNewProductFileToEmpty: a product file new in the slice maps to `""` in the product-only overlay.
- TestBaseOverlayNoProductOnlyOverlayWhenEntryDoesNotBuild: an entry that reads `does not build` gets no product-only line.

Vet sample:
- TestBaseOverlayVetSampleQuotesFirstFailureLine: vet stderr `# pkg\ninternal/x/b.go:20:12: w.quoted undefined` gives a sample paragraph quoting `internal/x/b.go:20:12: w.quoted undefined`. It does not quote `# pkg`.
- TestBaseOverlayVetSampleIsTheFirstFailureOfTheSection: the first failing vet run in section order is the one quoted, including a closure round that later builds. A later failure is not quoted.
- TestBaseOverlayVetSampleFromImporterFailure: when only an importer package's vet fails, its first line is the sample.
- TestBaseOverlayNoVetSampleWhenNoVetFails: when every vet exits zero, the section has no sample paragraph.
- TestBaseOverlayVetSampleSkipsExitCodeFallback: a vet that fails with empty output (text `go vet exit 1`) gives no sample.
- TestBaseOverlayVetSampleIsOneSafeLine: a 300-character line is cut to 200 characters, `|` becomes `/`, and a backtick becomes `'`, so the code span cannot break.

Existing tests that change because a failing vet now adds the sample paragraph:
- TestBaseOverlayBuildErrorIsOneShortLine: the exact body now also holds the sample paragraph, which is its own paragraph after the entry.
- TestBaseOverlayAllTogetherWhenEverySingleFileFails: the combined entry is still the last entry, and the sample paragraph follows it.
- TestBaseOverlayPerTestLinesCapAt20: with 25 Test functions in the changed test files, the section lists 20 per-test lines and one line saying 5 were left out (adj 669).

## Implement

1. In `internal/engine/baseoverlay.go` add `testNames(worktree, file string) []string`. It reads `filepath.Join(worktree, filepath.FromSlash(file))` with `os.ReadFile` and parses it with `go/parser` (add `go/ast` and `go/parser` imports, as `internal/engine/untestedcallsites.go` does). It returns the top-level functions with no receiver, no results and one parameter, whose name starts with `Test`, is not `TestMain`, and does not continue with a lowercase letter. Names are in source order. A file that cannot be read or parsed returns nil, so a failure is advisory and adds no notice.
2. In `baseOverlaySection`, after the entry's command is known (the `failed == false` path), build the per-test lines. For each file in `testFiles` (already sorted) whose `path.Dir` equals `path.Dir(p)` and that is not in `revertedTests`, add one line for each name from `testNames`: `"  - Test `NAME`: `go -C WT test -overlay OVERLAY -count=1 -run " + ShellWord(NAME) + " " + ShellWord(packageArg(p)) + "`"`. Put the pattern in one helper, `perTestRunPattern(name string) string`, so the form lives in one place. Append the lines to the same `entry` string, joined with `\n`, never as separate `entries` elements, because `len(entries)+1` numbers the overlay files. Count lines across the section and stop at the limit the owner sets. Then write "N more test lines were left out (ork lists at most LIMIT)." after the entries and importer lines, in the style of the importer left-out line.
3. In the same place, when `len(revertedTests) > 0` and the entry has a command, write `filepath.Join(tmpDir, fmt.Sprintf("overlay-%d-product.json", n))` with `writeOverlayJSON(file, map[string]string{key: replacement})`, the product file `p` only. Append a sub-line to the entry: `"  - Product file only, with this slice's tests kept (a test that needs a new symbol fails to build, which shows it is red): `go -C WT test -overlay PRODUCT_OVERLAY -count=1 PKG`"`. Do not vet it, and do not run it automatically. If the write fails, leave the sub-line out. A new product file maps to `""` as in `writeBaseCopy`.
4. Record the vet sample. Add a local `sample` string in `baseOverlaySection` and a `noteVet(output string)` that keeps only the first call. Call it for each failing `overlayVetOutput` in the per-file loop, closure rounds included. Replace the two `overlayBuildError` calls (importer and all-files) with `overlayVetOutput` plus `vetMessage`, call `noteVet` on a failure, and remove `overlayBuildError` once it is unused. `noteVet` takes the first non-empty line that does not start with `#`. It skips output that starts with `go vet exit `. It cuts the line to 200 runes, replaces `|` with `/` and a backtick with `'`.
5. After the entries, importer lines and left-out lines, write one paragraph when `sample != ""`: "Sample of a real `go vet` failure from these overlays: `LINE`". It is omitted when no vet fails. The existing intro and closing guidance keep their text, so the roles tests that pin them still pass.
6. Add the tests from Failing tests. Update `TestBaseOverlayBuildErrorIsOneShortLine` and `TestBaseOverlayAllTogetherWhenEverySingleFileFails` for the sample paragraph. Run each new test and watch it fail before step 1.
7. In `docs/design.md`, in the Base overlays bullet (`docs/design.md:2160-2216`), describe the per-test lines (form, the same-package and not-reverted rules, the limit, unreadable files), the product-only overlay (`overlay-N-product.json`, only when a test file is reverted, not vetted, red by compile error or assertion; adj 664), and the vet sample (adj 663). Cite S643, adj 655 and 632. Change the text only for these points.
8. Add the changelog entry with `slicer changelog add S643 --text "..." --root WT`. Do not edit `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Cap the per-test lines at baseOverlayLimit (20) for the whole section, with one line saying how many test lines were left out, as adj 604 and adj 625 do for files and importer lines (adj 669).
